context.content:
>I think the cloud backup services are basically a one way sync. What's on my computer is what will be on the server. If the file is deleted from the server, it will still be on my computer.

This is very very incorrect with Dropbox. If a file is deleted on Dropbox, the client will delete the copy on your computer. 

Dropbox may "think" that a file is deleted simply because it does not have access to it at some moment. This can happen for a number of reasons such as an antivirus program, you have the file open in a program or just a fluke.

As soon as this happens, DB deletes the cloud copy, thinking you meant to delete it. Then, next time it sees it on your computer it says "hey, this file was marked for deletion" and deletes the original. DB says themselves that this can happen. They claim there's nothing they can do about it. And in my opinion these situations are likely responsible for most instances when people's files go missing.
